title: Every divisor of a nonzero split polynomial splits over the same field
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $P,Q\in F[t]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Say that a polynomial $H\in F[t]$ splits over $F$ if $H=c\prod_{j\in J}(t-b_j)$ for a scalar $c\in F$ and a finite indexed family $(b_j)_{j\in J}$ in $F$; the empty product is $1$. Suppose $P\ne0$, $P$ splits over $F$, and $Q\mid P$ (that is, $P=QA$ for some $A\in F[t]$). Then $Q$ splits over $F$.

source.place: Tag 09HN, label lemma-normal-goes-up, proof: the polynomial inference “Then Q divides P in the polynomial ring E[x] ... Hence, if P splits completely over K, then so does Q.” This node isolates that generic polynomial inference, not the normal-extension statement. Splitting is the finite-factorization convention of section-normal (Tag 09HL), extended to constant polynomials by allowing the empty product.
